set.relationsSummary: This is the Reformed church of the Dutch East India Company. It took over the Christians the Portuguese left in the Moluccas. In Ceylon the Company's government turned its law against the Catholics, who are told in the entry on the Catholics of Dutch Ceylon. After 1815 it lived on in the Moluccas. The entry on Indonesian Christianity picks up its story in 1861.

livingEvidence.basis: The heirs of the Company's church, such as the Protestant Church of the Moluccas, are alive today. No dated present-day record is in hand. The entry continues in the tree's entry on Indonesian Christianity, which opens in 1861; the years 1815 to 1861 are not told. The descent grade rests on a modern study (Aritonang and Steenbrink, ch. 9), which tells Joseph Kam renewing the same church from 1815; the line from there to today's Moluccan church is not yet read from a source. The descent to today's church is graded lower than the link to the 1861 entry because the study tells the church's renewal after 1815, not its line to the present.
